mainTopic: Why the משנה repeats the rule about the signs of maturity, and the 'כיוצא בו' cases, especially holes in a כלי חרס.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion with one more answer. The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון and speaks about a girl past the age of maturity, and רבי שמעון does not accept רבא's חזקה. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה repeats that the upper sign cannot come before the lower sign. One answer is that the repeat shows the הלכה follows the רבנן. That is needed even though the majority usually wins, because פסוקים seem to support רבי מאיר. A second answer is that the line leads into the next משנה, 'כיוצא בו'. That משנה lists three one-way rules: holes in a כלי חרס, a limb with a nail and a bone, and מדרס compared with טמא מת. The גמרא then explains what the two hole sizes mean for מי חטאת and for a גסטרא. רב אסי teaches that the smaller 'lets out' size counts only for a גסטרא, because nobody patches a shard with another shard. Last, a ברייתא gives a test: set the pot in a tub of water to see whether water comes in.

steps.title: Another answer: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, past the age of maturity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers one more way to explain the earlier ברייתא. It follows רבי שמעון, it speaks about a girl past the age of maturity, and רבי שמעון does not accept רבא's חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: the ברייתא is רבי שמעון's view, it is talking about a girl after the age of maturity, and he does not accept רבא's assumption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion by giving another possible answer to a question it asked before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds a חזקה: a girl who reached the age of maturity is assumed to have grown the signs of maturity. If רבי שמעון does not accept that assumption, then even a girl past that age still needs to be checked. That explains why the ברייתא requires a check.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say', which introduces an alternate answer
After the age of maturity
A legal assumption about the way things normally are
He does not hold of it, meaning he does not accept it

steps.whatToRemember: The earlier question ends with this answer: רבי שמעון does not rely on רבא's חזקה, so a check is still needed even after the age of maturity.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: it is Rabbi Shimon,
and it is speaking of after the age of maturity,
and he does not hold of Rava's presumption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives one more alternate answer to a question from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא and a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבא's חזקה exists, it seemed a girl past maturity would never need a check.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון does not accept רבא's חזקה, so a check is needed even after the age of maturity.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat that the upper sign cannot come first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'because they said it is possible…' and asks why it is needed, since the first part of the משנה already said the upper sign cannot come before the lower one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Because they said it is possible, etc.' Why do I need this again? The first part of the משנה already taught it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and complains that the line just repeats something already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה already said the lower sign can come before the upper sign, but not the reverse. When the משנה states the same rule again as its reason, it looks extra. The גמרא assumes the משנה does not repeat itself without a purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Possible
Why do I need this again?
The first part of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the rule itself. It agrees the rule is true and only asks why the משנה says it twice.

phrases.english: "Because they said: It is possible, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the lower sign can come before the upper sign, but the upper sign can't come before the lower one.

phrases.english: Why do I need this again?
He already taught it in the first clause!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הָא תָּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated line in the משנה: 'מפני שאמרו אפשר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule was already stated in the רישא, so saying it again seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Suggested answer, siding with the רבנן, is called obvious
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the line repeats so the משנה can be taught without a name, following the רבנן. The גמרא rejects this as obvious, because when one sage disagrees with many, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say the reason is that the תנא wants to teach the unnamed משנה like the רבנן, that is obvious! When one sage disagrees with many, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer to its question and then immediately pushes it away as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה taught without a name (סתם משנה) usually shows what the הלכה is. Here, though, the רבנן are already a majority against רבי מאיר alone, so we would follow them anyway. Repeating the rule just to show this seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach it without a name (as a סתם משנה), which signals the הלכה
It is obvious
One sage against many: the הלכה follows the many

phrases.english: And if you would say: because he wants
to teach it unattributed, in accordance with the Rabbis —
phrases.notes: When a משנה states a rule with no name attached, that usually shows the הלכה follows it.

phrases.english: That is obvious!
An individual against the many — the halakha is like the many.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָעֵי לְמִסְתְּמַהּ כְּרַבָּנַן — פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to Step 2 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the repeat is there to fix the הלכה like the רבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The majority rule already gives that result, so the repeat would teach nothing new.

steps.title: It is needed, because פסוקים seem to support רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the suggested answer. Without the repeat, you might think רבי מאיר's reasoning is stronger because פסוקים support him. So the משנה teaches that the הלכה still follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי מאיר's reasoning makes more sense, since the פסוקים support him. So the משנה teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the answer it just pushed away. It explains why the majority rule alone would not have been enough here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The majority rule is normally enough. But the פסוקים quoted earlier, which mention breasts growing before hair, seem to support רבי מאיר's view that the upper sign can come first. That might have made us side with him even though he is alone. The unnamed משנה makes it clear that the הלכה follows the רבנן anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, meaning without this teaching you would have thought…
It is more logical
The פסוקים support him
So it teaches us something new

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even the 'majority wins' rule may need extra support when the minority view has strong backing from פסוקים.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
the reasoning of Rabbi Meir is more logical,
since the verses support him,
phrases.notes: These are the פסוקים quoted earlier on the daf, about breasts growing and hair sprouting (יחזקאל 16:7, 23:21).

phrases.english: therefore it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection in Step 3, which brings back the answer to Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא, explaining what mistaken idea we might otherwise have had
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because פסוקים support רבי מאיר, the הלכה might follow him even though he is alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unnamed משנה confirms that the הלכה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: Another answer: the line leads into the next case
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to why the line repeats: the משנה wants to go on and teach 'כיוצא בו', a similar case, and this line leads into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: it is repeated because the תנא wants to go on and teach 'similar to it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from Step 2: the repeat serves as a bridge to the next case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, the line is not about deciding the argument at all. Restating the rule sets up the next משנה, which opens with 'כיוצא בו', a case that works the same way. The repeat is there to make the flow of the משנה smooth.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach, meaning to state in the משנה
Similar to it, which introduces a parallel case

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the repeated line: (1) to show the הלכה follows the רבנן even though רבי מאיר has support from פסוקים; (2) to lead into the next case, 'כיוצא בו'.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
because he wants to teach "similar to it."
phrases.notes: This points to the next משנה, which begins with the words 'כיוצא בו'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִתְנֵי כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the question in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the wording as a link to what comes next
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The repeated line seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is there as a bridge to the next case, 'כיוצא בו'.

steps.title: Three cases where one thing always includes another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three cases where A always comes with B, but B can exist without A: holes in a כלי חרס, a limb with a nail and a bone, and מדרס compared with טמא מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similar to this: any clay vessel with a hole that lets liquid in also lets liquid out. But some holes let liquid out and do not let it in. Any limb that has a nail also has a bone. But some limbs have a bone and no nail. Anything that can become impure through מדרס can also become impure from a dead body. But some things can become impure from a dead body and cannot become impure through מדרס.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line that step 5 said the earlier phrase was leading into. The משנה gives three new examples of a one-way rule: A always comes with B, but B can come without A.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern matches the signs of maturity: the upper sign never comes without the lower one, but the lower one can come alone. Each example is built the same way: 'כל ... — ...' (every A has B), then 'ויש ...' (some have B without A).

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to it; a case built on the same pattern
An earthenware (clay) vessel
Lets liquid in / lets liquid out (said of a hole in the vessel)
A fingernail or toenail
Impurity a זב passes on by pressing on an item, such as sitting or lying on it
Impurity that comes from a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: Read each line in one direction only. 'Every A has B' does not mean 'every B has A'. The 'ויש' line is there to tell you the opposite is not always true.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Similar to it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the earlier rule that the upper sign of maturity never comes before the lower sign.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כְּלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיס — מוֹצִיא,
phrases.english: any clay vessel that lets in, lets out,
phrases.notes: He means a hole in the vessel. If liquid can come in through it, liquid can surely leak out through it.

phrases.english: and there is one that lets out but does not let in.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֵבֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ צִפּוֹרֶן — יֵשׁ בּוֹ עֶצֶם,
phrases.english: Any limb that has a nail in it has a bone in it,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ עֶצֶם וְאֵין בּוֹ צִפּוֹרֶן.
phrases.english: and there is one that has a bone in it but has no nail in it.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמִּטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס — מִטַּמֵּא טְמֵא מֵת,
phrases.english: Anything that becomes impure through treading becomes impure from a dead body,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁמִּטַּמֵּא טְמֵא מֵת — וְאֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס.
phrases.english: and there is something that becomes impure from a dead body but does not become impure through treading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the 'כיוצא בו' cases that step 5 said the repeated line was introducing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In each of the three pairs, the first thing always brings the second, but the second can exist without the first.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the earlier line in the משנה was not wasted words. It opens a whole list of cases built on the same one-way pattern.

steps.title: What the in-hole and out-hole mean for the clay vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first case. A hole that lets liquid in makes the vessel unfit for מי חטאת and also unfit as a גסטרא. A hole that only lets liquid out leaves it fit for מי חטאת, but it is still unfit as a גסטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hole that lets liquid in: the vessel is unfit for מי חטאת, and it is unfit as a גסטרא. A hole that only lets liquid out: the vessel is fit for מי חטאת, but it is unfit as a גסטרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical law behind the משנה's first example, the 'lets in / lets out' holes in a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bigger hole (מכניס) takes away the vessel's fitness for מי חטאת and also its use as a גסטרא. The smaller hole (מוציא) still disqualifies it as a גסטרא, but it can still be used for מי חטאת. This matches the one-way pattern: the bigger hole includes everything the small hole does, plus more.

keyTerms.meaning: The water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה, used for purifying people from טמא מת
A piece of a broken clay vessel that is still used to hold things
Unfit or disqualified
Fit or valid

steps.whatToRemember: A hole that lets liquid in is the bigger problem: the vessel loses both its use for מי חטאת and its use as a גסטרא. A hole that only lets liquid out costs only the גסטרא use.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Lets in: it is unfit for the water of purification,
and it is unfit as a shard.
phrases.notes: A גסטרא is a broken piece of a pot that people still use to hold things. With this hole, it can't even count as that.

phrases.english: Lets out: it is fit for the water of purification,
but it is unfit as a shard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical law behind the first case of the משנה in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole that lets liquid in disqualifies the vessel for מי חטאת and as a גסטרא. A hole that only lets liquid out disqualifies it as a גסטרא but leaves it fit for מי חטאת.

steps.title: The general hole size for a clay vessel is 'lets liquid in'
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the standard measure for a hole in a כלי חרס is כונס משקה. The smaller size, מוציא משקה, was said only about a גסטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: This is how it is taught. For a clay vessel, the hole size that counts is one that lets liquid in. The rule of a hole that only lets liquid out was said only about a broken shard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a general rule about which hole size makes a כלי חרס count as broken. He limits the smaller 'lets liquid out' size to a גסטרא alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed two hole sizes. רב אסי now says the bigger one, כונס משקה, is the normal measure for a כלי חרס. The smaller one, מוציא משקה, is a special rule only for a גסטרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A set measure or size
A hole big enough to let liquid come in from outside (the bigger hole)
A hole that only lets liquid leak out (the smaller hole)
'They teach': a set teaching that has been passed down

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but כונס משקה is the BIGGER hole. Liquid leaks out through even a tiny hole, while pushing water in from outside needs a larger opening.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said: They teach:
An earthenware vessel, its measure is a hole that lets liquid in,
phrases.notes: He means the size of hole that makes the vessel count as broken, so it is no longer טמא.

phrases.english: and they did not say 'lets liquid out'
except regarding a shard only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the two hole sizes from step 7 and sets the general rule for a כלי חרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס counts as broken with a כונס משקה hole. The מוציא משקה size applies only to a גסטרא.

steps.title: Why is a shard different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the smaller hole size is enough for a גסטרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב אסי's special rule for a גסטרא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other כלי חרס needs the bigger hole to count as broken. So why does a small leak already end a shard's use? The גמרא wants the logic.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A request for the logic behind a rule

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the גסטרא exception in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a גסטרא counts as broken with only a מוציא משקה hole.

steps.title: Nobody patches a shard with another shard
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן explains that people do not use one shard to fix another, so a leaking shard is useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said: Because people do not say, 'Bring a shard for a shard.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers the question. A shard is already the backup piece, so once it leaks, nobody bothers to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole pot that leaks a little can still be used by putting a shard under it to catch the drips. But a shard that leaks has no backup, because nobody puts a shard under a shard. So even a small leak ends its use.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Bring a shard for a shard': something people never say, since a leaking shard is just thrown out

steps.whatToRemember: A whole כלי חרס needs a כונס משקה hole to count as broken. A גסטרא counts as broken even with a מוציא משקה hole, because a leaking shard has no further use.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said:
Because people do not say:
'Bring a shard for a shard.'
phrases.notes: A shard usually goes under a leaking pot to catch drips. Nobody puts a second shard under a leaking shard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A leaking shard is never patched with another shard, so even a small leak ends its use.

steps.title: How to test whether a hole lets liquid in
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a test: put the pot into a tub of water. If water comes in, the hole is כונס משקה. If not, it is only מוציא משקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How do we check a clay vessel to know whether it has a hole that lets liquid in or not? Bring a tub full of water and put the pot into it. If water came in, we know it lets liquid in. If not, we know it only lets liquid out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a practical test for telling the two hole sizes apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the bigger hole (כונס משקה) is what matters for most vessels, we need a way to check it. Setting the pot in water shows whether water pushes in from outside. If no water comes in, the hole is only the smaller מוציא משקה size.

keyTerms.meaning: We check or test
A tub or large basin
A cooking pot
It is known for sure

steps.whatToRemember: Test: set the pot in a tub of water. Water comes in = כונס משקה. No water comes in = only מוציא משקה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How do we check an earthenware vessel

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם נִיקַּב בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה אִם לָאו?
phrases.english: to know whether it was pierced with a hole that lets liquid in, or not?
One brings a tub full of water,
and places the pot into it.
If it took in water, it is known that it lets liquid in,
and if not, it is known that it only lets liquid out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד בּוֹדְקִין כְּלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule about hole sizes to a practical way of measuring them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Put the pot in a tub of water. If water enters, the hole is כונס משקה. If not, it is only מוציא משקה.
